message:
feat(update): pin version comparison as a contract three runtimes read

The question "is this newer than what I have" gets asked in the server's
JavaScript, the Windows installer's C++, and the Android client's Kotlin. A
header cannot cross those boundaries, so what they share is the answers:
forty-six vectors in apps/shared/version_compare_vectors.txt, with the six
rules written above them, read by all three test suites. Drift now fails a
test instead of shipping quietly.

The C++ implementation moves out of installer_main.cpp -- where it was
file-local with no test at all -- into version_compare.hpp, which the updater
will need to give the same answer the installer gives. Extraction stays inside
C++; the other two runtimes get their own implementations, held to the same
vectors.

One deliberate behaviour change: a component saturates at 2147483647 instead
of wrapping. Three runtimes cannot be made to overflow alike, and nothing that
reaches the ceiling could be a real version string.

Each suite also checks antisymmetry on every vector, and fails if the vectors
file is empty -- otherwise a truncated file would read as a clean pass.

Verified with no RDP session (qwinsta: console active, rdp-tcp listening).
C++ 139 checks over 46 vectors, JS 95 checks over the same 46 with the whole
directory suite passing, Kotlin 2 tests. Installer relinks clean after the
extraction. No installer artifact produced, nothing installed or deployed.
